title: Keeping your speed up a ramp and through a drift
target: How to use the two boosts a vehicle earns in R.E.P.O.: the push a slope in the right angle window gives you, and the three graded tiers of boost a held drift pays out.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Ground with a slope or room to slide
Enough straight ahead to use the speed once you have it

steps.do: Treat a ramp as a place to gain speed rather than only as a way up, because the vehicle carries a boost that belongs to slopes alone.
steps.because: the ramp boost is a switch of its own on the vehicle (enableRampBoost)

steps.do: Read the slope before you commit, because only a certain window of angles pays out.
steps.because: the boost has a lowest and a highest slope angle (rampBoostMinSlopeAngle, rampBoostMaxSlopeAngle)

steps.do: Arrive with speed already built, because a slow crawl up a rise is not enough to start the boost.
steps.because: there is a lowest speed below which the boost does not apply (rampBoostMinSpeed)

steps.do: Expect the ground to do the pushing rather than the throttle, since the boost carries a force of its own.
steps.because: the boost has a force of its own (rampBoostForce)

steps.do: Turn with the speed you have instead of braking for the corner, because the vehicle sends existing speed in a new direction.
steps.because: the vehicle redirects the velocity it already has, with a strength of its own (velocityRedirectStrength)

steps.do: Watch the two ends of the vehicle when a slope begins, because the front and the back are checked separately for touching the ground.
steps.because: the front and the back have separate points for being on the ground (frontGroundedTransform, backGroundedTransform)

steps.do: Hold a slide to the end of your turn rather than straightening out early, because a drift boost is graded in three levels.
steps.because: drift boosts come in three levels, each reached at its own threshold (driftBoostLevel1Threshold, driftBoostLevel2Threshold, driftBoostLevel3Threshold)

steps.do: Keep the slide going while it is safe, because a higher level pushes harder than a lower one.
steps.because: each level carries its own forward boost and its own speed multiplier (driftBoostLevel1ForwardBoost, driftBoostLevel3SpeedBoostMultiplier)

steps.do: Use the effects to know which level you reached, because arriving at a level and holding it are drawn differently, and the light brightens with the level.
steps.because: each level has particles for reaching it and for holding it, and its own light brightness (driftBoostLevel1ReachedParticles, driftBoostLevel2Particles, boostLightIntensityLevel3)

steps.do: Plan where the boost ends, because a level lasts a set time rather than as long as you like.
steps.because: each level lasts for its own duration (driftBoostLevel2Duration)

commonMistakes: Crawling up a rise and expecting the boost, when it has a lowest speed.
Taking a slope that is too gentle or too steep, which sits outside the angle window.
Straightening out of a slide early and settling for the lowest level.
Braking into a corner instead of turning the speed you already have.
Spending the boost on open ground with nothing to reach.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
